question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

A soothe voice must convey both confidence and intimacy, qualities which can be attributed to a few key components.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A soothe voice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word required before the noun "voice" is an adjective, but "soothe" is a verb (to calm, to relieve). The correct adjective form is "soothing". (शांत करने वाला / सुखदायक)

◦ Correct: A soothing voice must convey both confidence and intimacy, qualities which can be attributed to a few key components.

• Rule: A word placed between an article (a/an/the) and a noun must be an adjective, not a verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "few key components" is correct — "a few" with a plural countable noun.

• Option 3 "convey both confidence" is correct — "both ... and" joins two nouns (confidence and intimacy).

• Option 4 "which can be" is a correct relative clause referring to "qualities".

NOTE

• Verb → adjective forms: soothe → soothing, please → pleasing, annoy → annoying, tire → tiring.

• "Soothing" describes something that produces calm; "soothed" describes the person who feels calm.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Empathetic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Merciless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Empathetic" means showing an ability to understand and share the feelings of another; compassionate. (सहानुभूतिपूर्ण)

• Its antonym is "Merciless", which means showing no mercy or compassion; cruel and pitiless. (निर्दयी / बेरहम)

◦ Example: The empathetic nurse comforted the patient, unlike the merciless guard who ignored him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Lonely" (अकेला) means without companions — unrelated to feeling for others.

• Option 3 "Charismatic" (करिश्माई) means having a compelling charm that inspires devotion.

• Option 4 "Frustrated" (निराश) means feeling annoyed because of an inability to change something.

NOTE

• Synonyms of empathetic: compassionate, sympathetic, understanding, considerate, sensitive.

• Antonyms of empathetic: merciless, callous, indifferent, unfeeling, apathetic, heartless.

• Do not confuse empathy (feeling *with* someone) and sympathy (feeling *for* someone).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The police inspector knows the ins and outs of the murder case.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. full details.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "ins and outs" means all the detailed facts, intricacies or complete particulars of something. (सारी बारीकियाँ / पूरा विवरण)

◦ Correct sense: The police inspector knows the full details of the murder case.

◦ Example: After ten years in the department, she knows the ins and outs of the procedure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "laws", Option 2 "all the witnesses" and Option 3 "lawyers and judges" are literal distractors drawn from the courtroom context; none of them is the meaning of the idiom.

• An idiom must be taken as a whole; its meaning cannot be worked out from the individual words.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about complete knowledge: "know something inside out", "know something like the back of one's hand", "at one's fingertips", "chapter and verse".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

He told me / that he goes / to the market / to buy a laptop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. that he goes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The principal clause is in the past tense ("He told me"). By the rule of the sequence of tenses, the verb in the subordinate (reported) clause must also move to a past form. So "goes" (present) must become "went" (past).

◦ Correct: He told me that he went to the market to buy a laptop.

• Rule: Past principal clause → past subordinate clause (goes → went, is → was, will → would, has → had).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "He told me" is correct — "tell" takes a direct object (me) without a preposition.

• Option 3 "to the market" is the correct prepositional phrase of destination.

• Option 2 "to buy a laptop" is a correct infinitive of purpose.

NOTE

• Exception to the sequence of tenses: if the subordinate clause states a universal truth, habitual fact or historical fact, the present tense is retained — e.g., "He said that the earth moves round the sun."

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence.

The energetic kitten is playful after having his breakfast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. its.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "kitten" is an animal whose sex is not specified, so the neuter possessive adjective "its" must be used before the noun "breakfast", not the masculine "his".

◦ Correct: The energetic kitten is playful after having its breakfast.

• Rule: A possessive adjective (my, your, his, her, its, our, their) comes directly before a noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "it’s" is the contraction of "it is / it has" — it is not possessive, so "it’s breakfast" would wrongly read "it is breakfast".

• Options 3 "it" and 4 "it is" cannot stand before a noun as a possessive.

NOTE

• Remember the classic distinction: its = belonging to it (no apostrophe); it’s = it is / it has (with apostrophe).

◦ "The dog wagged its tail." / "It’s raining outside."

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

It is commonly believed / that Democracy is / the best form / of the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of the government.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "government" is used in a general/abstract sense (a system of governing), not about one particular government. Hence the definite article "the" must be dropped.

◦ Correct: It is commonly believed that Democracy is the best form of government.

• Rule: No article is used before an abstract or general noun used in its widest sense — e.g., "form of government", "freedom of speech", "man is mortal".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "It is commonly believed" is a correct impersonal passive structure.

• Option 3 "that Democracy is" is a correct noun clause.

• Option 4 "the best form" correctly uses "the" with a superlative degree.

NOTE

• "The" IS used when the noun is particularised — "the government of India resigned". It is omitted for the general concept — "the best form of government".

question:
Four words of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a spelling error.

Ozone is a reactiev gas that is not only important in protecting us from harmful ultraviolet radiation but is also a greenhouse gas and, at high smog-level concentrations, harmful to human health and vegetation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. reactiev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reactiev" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "reactive", meaning readily taking part in chemical reactions; responsive to a stimulus. (प्रतिक्रियाशील)

• Spelling key: RE + AC + TIVE (the ending is "-ive", as in active, passive, sensitive) — never "-iev".

◦ Correct: Ozone is a reactive gas that is not only important in protecting us from harmful ultraviolet radiation ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "radiation" (the emission of energy as waves/particles — विकिरण), "concentrations" (the amount of a substance in a given volume — सांद्रता) and "vegetation" (plant life of a region — वनस्पति) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Adjectives ending in -ive: active, passive, reactive, sensitive, creative, effective, massive.

• Related words: react (verb), reaction (noun), reactive (adjective), reactivity (noun).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He said that I have finished my work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. he had finished his work.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a sentence of indirect (reported) speech. Two changes are needed:

◦ Pronoun change: the reported pronoun must agree with the subject of the reporting verb ("He said"), so "I ... my" becomes "he ... his".

◦ Tense change: the reporting verb "said" is past, so the present perfect "have finished" shifts to the past perfect "had finished".

◦ Correct: He said that he had finished his work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "he has finished his work" keeps the present perfect and violates the sequence of tenses.

• Option 3 "I had finished my work" fails to change the pronouns.

• Option 4 "he was finished his work" is grammatically wrong (a wrong passive/active mixture).

NOTE

• Direct → Indirect tense shifts: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; present perfect → past perfect; past simple → past perfect; will → would; can → could; may → might.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word.

A piano teacher described an interesting encountar she had with a young lady who came to inquire about music lessons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. encountar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Encountar" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "encounter", meaning an unexpected or brief meeting; to come across something/someone. (मुठभेड़ / सामना)

• Spelling key: EN + COUN + TER (the ending is "-ter", not "-tar").

◦ Correct: A piano teacher described an interesting encounter she had with a young lady ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "interesting" (arousing curiosity), "inquire" (to ask for information) and "piano" (a keyboard musical instrument) are all correctly spelt.

• Note that both "inquire" (British preference) and "enquire" are acceptable spellings.

NOTE

• Common "-ter" endings often misspelt as "-tar": encounter, character, register, centre/center, calendar (this one really is "-dar").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

The executives were running around in circles, without any success.
option_4: Putting efforts into something that does not give a worthwhile result
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Putting efforts into something that does not give a worthwhile result.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to run around in circles" (also "go round in circles") means to work hard at something without making any real progress; to waste effort fruitlessly. (व्यर्थ प्रयास करना / बिना प्रगति के भागदौड़ करना)

◦ The clue "without any success" in the sentence confirms this meaning.

◦ Example: We kept running around in circles in the meeting and reached no decision.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Achieving maximum mileage" suggests great benefit — the opposite of the idiom.

• Option 2 "Suffering huge profits and losses" is self-contradictory and unrelated.

• Option 3 "Successfully accomplishing the target" is the direct opposite of the idiom.

NOTE

• Idioms of futile effort: "beat about the bush", "flog a dead horse", "cry over spilt milk", "a wild goose chase", "barking up the wrong tree".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Many great people born in that small village.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. were born.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To be born" is always used in the passive voice (be + born). The sentence as printed has no auxiliary verb, so it is incomplete.

• The subject "Many great people" is plural, and the action refers to the past, so the correct form is "were born".

◦ Correct: Many great people were born in that small village.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "was born" is singular and does not agree with the plural subject "Many great people".

• Option 3 "is born" is singular and in the present tense, unsuitable for a past event.

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the sentence needs an auxiliary.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: "many + plural noun" always takes a plural verb (Many students are ...), whereas "many a + singular noun" takes a singular verb (Many a student is ...).

question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

He was carefullest while stealing the crown jewels.
option_1: He was more careful while stealing the crown jewels.
option_2: He was most carefuller while stealing the crown jewels.
option_3: He was carefuller while stealing the crown jewels.
option_4: He was most careful while stealing the crown jewels.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. He was most careful while stealing the crown jewels.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Careful" is a two-syllable adjective ending in -ful, so its degrees are formed with more / most, never with the endings "-er / -est".

◦ Positive: careful → Comparative: more careful → Superlative: most careful.

• "Carefullest" and "carefuller" are therefore both wrong forms; the intended superlative sense gives "most careful".

◦ Correct: He was most careful while stealing the crown jewels.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more careful" is a valid form but expresses the comparative degree, whereas the original "carefullest" clearly intends the superlative.

• Option 2 "most carefuller" is a double comparative/superlative — always incorrect.

• Option 3 "carefuller" is not an English word.

NOTE

• Rule of degrees: one-syllable adjectives take -er/-est (tall–taller–tallest); two-syllable adjectives ending in -ful, -ous, -ing, -ed and all three-syllable adjectives take more/most (more useful, most beautiful).

• Never combine both — "more better", "most easiest" are wrong.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Hesitate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Falter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hesitate" means to pause or hold back in doubt or uncertainty before acting or speaking. (हिचकिचाना / झिझकना)

• "Falter" means to hesitate, waver or lose confidence/strength, which is its closest synonym. (लड़खड़ाना / हिचकना)

◦ Example: She did not hesitate/falter for a moment before giving her answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Blabber" (बकबक करना) means to talk foolishly or reveal secrets by talking too much.

• Option 2 "Recoil" (पीछे हटना) means to draw back suddenly in fear or disgust — a physical/emotional shrinking rather than doubt.

• Option 3 "Conceal" (छिपाना) means to hide something from view.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hesitate: falter, waver, vacillate, dither, pause, demur, be reluctant.

• Antonyms of hesitate: decide, resolve, plunge, proceed confidently.

• Related noun: hesitation; adjective: hesitant.

question:
The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors.

We can also contribute to presarvation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.
option_1: We can also contribute to presarvation of water bodies by not dumpeing our garbage in them.
option_2: We can also contribute to preservation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.
option_3: We can also contribut to presarvation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.
option_4: We can also contribute to presarvation of water bodies by not dumping our garbag in them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. We can also contribute to preservation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 2 spells every word correctly — "contribute", "preservation", "dumping" and "garbage".

• The key error in the given sentence is "presarvation", whose correct spelling is "preservation" — the act of keeping something in its original state. (संरक्षण)

◦ Spelling key: PRE + SER + VA + TION (from "preserve"), never "-sar-".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "presarvation" and "dumpeing" (correct: dumping — a silent "e" is dropped before "-ing").

• Option 3 misspells "contribut" (correct: contribute) and "presarvation".

• Option 4 misspells "presarvation" and "garbag" (correct: garbage).

NOTE

• Word family: preserve (verb) → preservation (noun) → preservative (noun/adjective) → preservationist.

• Spelling rule: for verbs ending in a silent "-e", drop the "e" before "-ing": dumping is regular, but come → coming, make → making, write → writing.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Call it a day
option_1: To have the greatest day ever
option_4: To refer to something as something else
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To stop working.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "call it a day" means to stop working on something (for the day); to decide that enough has been done and finish. (काम बंद कर देना / दिन का काम समाप्त करना)

◦ Example: It was already 9 p.m., so the team decided to call it a day.

◦ It can also mean to end an activity or career permanently — "After 20 years in the game, the veteran called it a day."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To have the greatest day ever" is a literal misreading of "day".

• Option 3 "To be very straightforward" corresponds to idioms like "call a spade a spade".

• Option 4 "To refer to something as something else" is the literal sense of the verb "call", not the idiom.

NOTE

• Related idioms with "call": "call it quits" (to stop/give up), "call a spade a spade" (to speak plainly), "call the shots" (to be in charge), "call off" (to cancel).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Stern
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Lenient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Stern" means serious, strict and severe, especially in enforcing discipline or punishment. (कठोर / सख्त)

• Its antonym is "Lenient", meaning merciful, tolerant and not strict in punishing. (उदार / नरम)

◦ Example: The stern principal was replaced by a lenient one who rarely punished anybody.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Stable" (स्थिर) means firm and not likely to change — unrelated to strictness.

• Option 2 "Sincere" (ईमानदार) means genuine and free from pretence.

• Option 3 "Profound" (गहन) means very great, intense or showing deep insight.

NOTE

• Synonyms of stern: strict, severe, harsh, rigorous, austere, unyielding, grim.

• Antonyms of stern: lenient, mild, gentle, indulgent, tolerant, kind, permissive.

• (In nautical use, the "stern" is also the rear part of a ship — a different meaning altogether.)

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

His older brothers were quite willing that he should went to sea.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. go to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal auxiliary "should", the verb must always be in its base form (V1). "Went" is the past form (V2) and is therefore wrong.

◦ Correct: His older brothers were quite willing that he should go to sea.

• Rule: Modal + V1 — can go, will go, may go, must go, should go.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had go to" mixes an auxiliary with a base verb and is ungrammatical after "should".

• Option 2 "have gone in" gives the wrong preposition ("go to sea" is the fixed expression) and the wrong form after "should".

• Option 3 "gone to" (V3) cannot follow "should" without "have".

NOTE

• "Go to sea" is an idiomatic expression meaning "to become a sailor". Compare "go to school", "go to church", "go to bed" — no article is used in such idiomatic phrases.

• Modals (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to) are never followed by "-s", "-ed" or "-ing" forms.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’.

It is true that learning English is essential for professionals to survived the national and international competitions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. for surviving.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The printed form "to survived" is wrong, because after the infinitive marker "to" only the base form (V1) can come — never the past form (V2).

• The sentence already contains "for professionals"; the best correction supplied is the prepositional phrase "for surviving" (preposition + gerund), which expresses purpose smoothly.

◦ Correct: It is true that learning English is essential for professionals for surviving the national and international competitions.

• Rule: A preposition is always followed by a gerund (V-ing), not an infinitive — "for surviving", "in winning", "on completing".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to be survive" is doubly wrong — "be" cannot be followed by the base verb "survive".

• Option 2 "having to survive" changes the meaning to compulsion and does not fit the structure.

• Option 3 "No improvement required" is wrong because "to survived" is clearly ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Common preposition + gerund combinations: good at swimming, interested in reading, fond of singing, afraid of failing, insist on going, look forward to meeting.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The tigress that was killed by the villagers was not only a man-eater, ________ a mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. but also.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Not only ... but also" is a correlative conjunction and must always be used as a complete pair. Since the sentence begins with "not only a man-eater", the blank must be filled with "but also".

◦ Correct: The tigress ... was not only a man-eater, but also a mother.

• The two elements joined must be parallel — here, both are noun phrases ("a man-eater" / "a mother").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "but" alone leaves the pair incomplete.

• Option 3 "and" cannot follow "not only".

• Option 4 "but often" is not a correlative pairing with "not only".

NOTE

• Common correlative conjunctions: not only ... but also; either ... or; neither ... nor; both ... and; whether ... or; no sooner ... than; hardly ... when; scarcely ... when; such ... that; so ... that.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Spill the beans
option_2: Behave or speak in a rash manner
option_4: To reveal a secret information unintentionally
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To reveal a secret information unintentionally.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "spill the beans" means to disclose a secret, often accidentally or prematurely. (राज़ खोल देना / भेद खोलना)

◦ Example: We wanted to keep the party a surprise, but Rohit spilled the beans.

• Its origin is traced to ancient voting with beans in jars — knocking the jar over revealed the result before time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Excellent health" corresponds to idioms like "hale and hearty" or "in the pink".

• Option 2 "Behave or speak in a rash manner" fits "shoot from the hip" or "fly off the handle".

• Option 3 "Things always get worse" suggests "go from bad to worse" or "add fuel to the fire".

NOTE

• Idioms about revealing secrets: "let the cat out of the bag", "blow the whistle", "give the game away", "blurt out".

• Opposite idioms (keeping quiet): "keep it under wraps", "keep mum", "button one's lip".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Photosynthesis is the _______(1) used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. The process chemically _______(2) carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. The chemical reaction often ______(3) on a pigment called chlorophyll, which gives plants their green colour. Photosynthesis is also the __________(4) our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the __________(5) air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. process.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "process" means a series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end. (प्रक्रिया)

• Photosynthesis is indeed a step-by-step biochemical process by which plants convert light energy into chemical energy.

◦ Correct: Photosynthesis is the process used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy.

• The very next sentence of the passage begins "The process chemically ...", which confirms that the first blank must be "process".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "guess" (an estimate without sufficient information) makes no sense for a scientific mechanism.

• Option 3 "chaos" (complete disorder) contradicts the orderly nature of photosynthesis.

• Option 4 "area" (a region or space) does not fit "used by plants ... to turn sunlight into energy".

NOTE

• Contextual clue technique: in cloze tests, always scan the following sentences — a repeated word ("The process") is the strongest signal for the correct answer.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Photosynthesis is the _______(1) used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. The process chemically _______(2) carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. The chemical reaction often ______(3) on a pigment called chlorophyll, which gives plants their green colour. Photosynthesis is also the __________(4) our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the __________(5) air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. converts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Convert" means to change something into a different form or substance. (परिवर्तित करना)

• The structure "converts X into Y" exactly matches the sentence: "converts carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen".

◦ Correct: The process chemically converts carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen.

• The singular subject "The process" also requires the singular verb "converts".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "exceeds" (to go beyond a limit) does not take "into" and gives no sense here.

• Option 3 "crates" means to pack in wooden boxes — clearly unrelated (do not confuse it with "creates").

• Option 4 "bows" (to bend forward in respect) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Verbs commonly followed by "into": convert into, translate into, transform into, divide into, turn into, change into.

• Chemistry of photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Photosynthesis is the _______(1) used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. The process chemically _______(2) carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. The chemical reaction often ______(3) on a pigment called chlorophyll, which gives plants their green colour. Photosynthesis is also the __________(4) our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the __________(5) air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. relies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rely on" means to depend on something/someone for support or success. (निर्भर होना)

• The blank is immediately followed by the preposition "on", and among the options only "relies" collocates naturally with "on".

◦ Correct: The chemical reaction often relies on a pigment called chlorophyll ...

• The singular subject "The chemical reaction" also needs the singular verb "relies".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "creates" would need a direct object, not "on" ("creates a pigment", not "creates on a pigment").

• Option 3 "hopes" and Option 4 "wants" attribute human desire to a chemical reaction and do not take "on".

NOTE

• Preposition collocations: rely on, depend on, insist on, comment on, concentrate on.

• Chlorophyll is the green pigment inside chloroplasts that absorbs mainly blue and red light and reflects green light, giving leaves their colour.

question:

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
Photosynthesis is the _______(1) used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. The process chemically _______(2) carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. The chemical reaction often ______(3) on a pigment called chlorophyll, which gives plants their green colour. Photosynthesis is also the __________(4) our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the __________(5) air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reason.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reason" means the cause or explanation for something happening. (कारण)

• Photosynthesis releases oxygen, and that is exactly why the Earth has an oxygen-rich atmosphere — so "reason" fits the causal sense of the sentence.

◦ Correct: Photosynthesis is also the reason our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "goal" (an aim one works towards) would wrongly imply that photosynthesis has an intention.

• Option 2 "sense" does not fit the structure "is also the sense our planet is ...".

• Option 4 "occasion" means a particular time or event, not a cause.

NOTE

• "The reason (why/that) ..." is a standard structure; the "why" is often omitted in informal writing, as in this passage.

• Earth's atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and 1% other gases — the oxygen being largely of photosynthetic origin.

Photosynthesis is the _______(1) used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. The process chemically _______(2) carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. The chemical reaction often ______(3) on a pigment called chlorophyll, which gives plants their green colour. Photosynthesis is also the __________(4) our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the __________(5) air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. surrounding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Surrounding" means being all around something; encircling. (आसपास का / चारों ओर का)

• Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air immediately around them, so "the surrounding air" is the precise expression.

◦ Correct: Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the surrounding air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "afar" is an adverb (from a distance) and cannot modify the noun "air".

• Option 2 "distant" (far away) contradicts the fact that gas exchange happens right at the leaf surface.

• Option 4 "close" would need "close-by" or "nearby" to work as a modifier and is not idiomatic before "air".

NOTE

• Stomata (singular: stoma) are tiny pores, mostly on the lower surface of leaves, guarded by guard cells; they control gas exchange and transpiration.
